title: Raheem Sterling joins Dutch club Feyenoord after Chelsea exit
content:
Raheem Sterling  has joined Dutch club Feyenoord until the end of the season after leaving Chelsea.

Sterling, 31, departed Chelsea at the end of January after a mutual agreement was reached to terminate his contract 18 months early.

The first opportunity for the former Liverpool and Manchester City forward to make his debut for his new club will be at home against Go Ahead Eagles in the Eredivisie on Sunday.

“As a free agent, I’ve had, for the first time in a long time, the opportunity to control the next step in my career,” Sterling, who spent last season on loan at Arsenal, said upon completing the move.

“I wanted to take my time to speak with clubs and their head coaches to better understand the role they envisioned for me and ensure that I can add real value in this next chapter. Having spoken in great detail with CEO Dennis te Kloese and (Feynoord coach) Robin (van Persie), I’m confident that Feyenoord is a place I can be happy and establish myself as a valued member of the team.

“Playing abroad is a whole new challenge for me — and one I’m ready to embrace. Honestly, I’m just excited to get started.”

Van Persie said of Sterling’s arrival: “His football resume speaks for itself: he’s a player whose qualities can change the outcome of a game without a doubt.”

He had made 81 appearances for Chelsea but had not made a competitive appearance for them since May 2024 and this term had been training away from the first team. The winger was the club’s highest-paid player, on more than £300,000 a week.

Sterling joined Chelsea from Manchester City in the summer of 2022 for £47.5million ($65.5m). He fell out of favour with former head coach Enzo Maresca — who was replaced by Liam Rosenior in January — in the summer of 2024 and went on loan to Arsenal for the 2024-25 season. The forward failed to make an impact, however, scoring once in 28 games and only starting in seven league matches.

Sterling has made 396 Premier League appearances after breaking through from Liverpool’s under-18s and moving to City in 2015.

The last of his 82 England caps came as a late substitute in the 2022 World Cup quarter-final defeat by France in Qatar.

Feyenoord are second in the Eredivisie, 17 points behind leaders PSV, and are managed by former Manchester United and Arsenal striker Van Persie. The club are 16-time Dutch champions, most recently in 2023.

A top-two finish in the Eredivisie would see Feyenoord qualify for next season’s Champions League.
